2002/03.standingsNote: Top 6 only (from Belgrave Harriers match report)

2004/05.punditry: Ranelagh won their first Women's Division 1 title in the league's 26-year history, holding off defending champions Belgrave despite the Belles winning two of the four matches.

2006/07.punditry: Belgrave's Chrissie Wellington, fresh from winning the World Triathlon Age Group Championships, won Race 2 at Lightwater with teammate Catherine Bryson second - the Belles' first 1-2 in years. The following year Wellington would win the first of her four Ironman World Championships.

2012/13.standingsNote: Top 6 only (from Belgrave Harriers match report)

2025/26.punditry: [BEL](@club:BEL) won their third consecutive title, completing the double with the men's team. Only [THH](@club:THH) in [2009/10](@season:2009/10) have done that before. · The double takes [BEL](@club:BEL) past [THH](@club:THH) to the top of the all-time combined titles table with 19. · [Ruby Carter](@athlete:H/W) won the individual championship, finishing first in two of her three races. · [HHH](@club:HHH) finished runners-up for the second year running.

2026/27.punditry: [BEL](@club:BEL) are on a three-year title winning streak and will be hoping to make it four in a row. · [VAC](@club:VAC) make their first ever appearance in Division 1. · [REI](@club:REI) bounce straight back after one season in Division 2. · [W/W](@club:W/W) return to the top flight for the first time since [2023/24](@season:2023/24).
